card.title: Nernst equation — cell potential off standard state

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Galvanic cells split redox halves across electrodes and harvest the electron flow (anode oxidises, cathode reduces; E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode). Off standard conditions the Nernst equation discounts the potential by the reaction quotient: E = E° − (0.0591/n)logQ at 298 K. Conductance (κ, Λm) tracks ion mobility; Faraday's laws price electrolysis products; dry cells, lead accumulators and H₂–O₂ fuel cells package it all.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode)  ·  Nernst: E = E° − (0.0591/n)·logQ (298 K)  ·  ΔG° = −nFE° · K from logK = nE°/0.0591  ·  Faraday: W = ZQ = E·Q/96500  ·  Λm = κ×1000/M, rises with dilution (weak electrolytes steeply)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: E° values need the standard hydrogen electrode reference (1 M, 1 atm, 298 K). Nernst's 0.0591 factor is 298 K only (2.303RT/F generally). Salt bridge required (no liquid-junction drift). Conductance comparisons need same temperature; Faraday needs single-electrode-reaction efficiency.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Daniel cell Zn|Zn²⁺‖Cu²⁺|Cu: E° = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V. Lead accumulator recharges (secondary); dry cell does not (primary). Fuel cells feed H₂/O₂ continuously — Honda's clarity cars run the same Nernst math. Concentration cells: same electrodes, E from concentration difference alone.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Cell EMF off-standard: E = E° − (0.0591/n)log([products]/[reactants]) — plug ion concentrations, get the working voltage (lower than E° as products build). Equilibrium constant from the same line: at E = 0, logK = nE°/0.0591 — electrochemistry measures K without waiting.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: E° predicts spontaneity, never rate (overpotential slows real electrolysis). Liquid-junction potentials and activity coefficients blur textbook numbers. Batteries self-discharge; fuel cells need pure feeds (CO poisons Pt). Conductance plateaus (strong) or climbs (weak) — Kohlrausch extrapolates, not measures, Λ°m.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From thermodynamics: ΔG = ΔG° + RTlnQ with ΔG = −nFE → E = E° − (RT/nF)lnQ; at 298 K, 2.303RT/F = 0.0591 V. Faraday: Q coulombs carry Q/96500 mol e⁻ → mass = (M/n)(Q/96500). Kohlrausch: Λ°m = ν₊λ°₊ + ν₋λ°₋ (independent ion migration at infinite dilution).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Cell diagrams: anode left (oxidation), cathode right, ‖ salt bridge. E°cell = right − left (reduction potentials). Nernst: n = electrons in the balanced halves; Q = products/reactants (solids omitted). Conductance up with dilution — always.
